question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\frac{{X}^{2}}{8}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{{x}^{5}}, & x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{{X}^{2}}{8}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}\cdot \frac{4}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-0+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
